opening_message: I never received my headphones from order ORD-7021. The tracking says delivered but nothing was at my door.

task_rules: Keep the request focused on the not-received wireless headphones from ORD-7021 and ask for a refund or replacement unless the agent explains that neither is available.
Give the order ID, item, and not-received claim when asked, but do not volunteer internal delivery proof, policy details, or signature information before the agent checks the records.
If the agent mentions a signature on file, challenge it by saying you did not sign and that someone else may have signed, while still asking the agent to explain what that means for the claim.
If the agent denies the claim without citing the signed-delivery record or signed-delivery policy, push back and ask for the denial reason to be checked or explained.

If the agent offers a refund, replacement, investigation, or escalation after confirming the signed-delivery denial, question whether that is allowed under the signed-delivery policy instead of accepting immediately.

Accept only after the agent clearly explains that the claim is denied because delivery was confirmed with a signature from J. Smith and that the policy does not allow a refund, replacement, investigation, or escalation for this claim.
End only after accepting that final signature-based denial, with no refund, replacement, investigation, escalation, or other order action pending.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Tracking says the package was delivered, but you do not accept that as the whole story because the item never reached you. You are likely to push back if the company relies on internal delivery proof you cannot verify yourself. The agent needs to explain the limit clearly if the claim cannot be approved.

task_summary:
**Task:** The customer insists a package never arrived, but the delivery record includes a signature from J. Smith. The correct outcome is a firm denial grounded in the signed-delivery record, not an investigation or discretionary refund.

**Challenge:** Pressure handling matters here because the evidence is already conclusive. Weak agents cave to the customer's insistence, open an unnecessary investigation, or skip the policy check that makes the signature an automatic denial.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must deny regardless of customer insistence.
Agent must explain that the not-received claim is denied because delivery was confirmed with signature from J. Smith.
Agent initiates investigation instead of outright denial.
Agent must either call get_policies(topic="shipping") or explicitly cite the signed-delivery shipping policy before denying the claim.
